focus: Friendship Day + Freedom Weekend + Raksha Bandhan

strategy:
Azaadi From Average.

Commercial job: Recruit whole friend groups on Friendship Day; sell annuals over Freedom Weekend with a 2028 price lock instead of a deeper discount; remove the commitment objection for newcomers with a break-up clause; protect the festive-season renewal book with freezes. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit, never to a class count.

Newcomer: No Strings Attached (“Commitment issues? Same. Here’s a membership with a break-up clause.”). Clients with 5+ visits in month one buy again at 93.5%. A break-up clause costs almost nothing (few use it) and answers the objection the desk hears most: “what if I can’t keep it up?”.

Spot: Price Ki Azaadi (Freedom From Price Hikes) (“Freedom from price hikes. Lock your 2028 renewal at 2027 prices.”). A price lock costs nothing in 2027 and answers the renewal-price objection a year early. It sells the annual on certainty, not depth, and every lock is a 2028 renewal already in the book.

Referral: Squad Goals, Squat Goals (“Your squad. Our studio. Matching socks, obviously.”). Referrals convert at 22–76%; friends who start together come together. A free group class lowers the bar for the nervous friend, and the member is paid only when someone buys.

Renewal: Freedom to Pause (Not Quit) (“Pause for Ganpati. Pause for Diwali. Just don’t quit.”). Members lapse in Sep–Nov when travel breaks the habit. A freeze keeps them paying and coming back instead of cancelling; freezes have no cash cost, so the cash discount stays at the standard 15%.
notes: Build: 82 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹9.1L; 90 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹21.0L; 40 winbacks = ₹4.6L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹3.4L. Offers carry ₹29.8L (78% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.
